changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 6 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8653-listview-title-retired-rowactiondefs-pinned.md`

- names `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `title` — **retired.** `ListView` resolved its export filename through `schema.label || (schema as any).title`. `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `ListViewSchema` refuses `title` **by name** (`unrecognized_keys: ['title']`) while `ObjectGridPropsSchema` **accepts** it; `packages/types` mirrors the platform contract rather than ruling over it, so declaring `title` on `ListViewSchema` would have made this repo accept what the platform save gate rejects. That asymmetry is also why objectui#6639 could take the *declare* branch for `ObjectGridSchema.title` one package over and this site could not. A parse-based census of `apps/ examples/ content/` and `packages/` found **zero** `list-view` nodes authoring `title`, so the retirement costs no author a filename. Over that same corpus the instrument reports **three** `object-grid` nodes carrying the key: **two authored** ones, both in `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, plus one that is not authored at all — `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` composes `title: schema.table?.title` onto a grid node it builds, so it is a producer writing the key rather than an author declaring it. `ObjectGrid`'s own `title` reads are untouched — they remain declared, ruled and read.

### `.changeset/object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.md`

- names `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What was measured.** Every reading was taken on the `object-view` node renderer (`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`, registered by `plugin-view/src/index.tsx`) with `schema.objectName` / `schema.layout` as the positive controls of the same `schema.KEY` query, so each zero is a reading; the repo-wide census of `viewTabBar` finds the key in no source file outside `@object-ui/types` (two doc tables listed it as authorable and are corrected here). The spec side was read through the installed pin (`@objectstack/spec@17.2.0`, `ui` entry, 117 exported object schemas walked; control keys `objectName` / `columns` / `navigation` / `listViews` hit): the three spec-modelled keys are optional slots on `ListViewSchema` and `ObjectListViewSchema`; the six local keys have no spec slot anywhere.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `ad0310fb5` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1706 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2308 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36457619848)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0d122bf345c88d43a7d383ce2bff804fad7ad7a3`

This is an in-seat review. The diff is one render helper, two call sites, a pin file, a changeset, a dated note, and the README and docs pages (6 files, +190 −2), `Clause-②: no`, executing triage `5872733337`. I read the whole diff against `main` `ad0310fb57`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The fix is gated on `create` alone.**
   - `renderCreateSurface` returns `null` unless `formMode === 'create'`.
   - It draws `renderModalForm()` for `layout === 'modal'` and `renderDrawerForm()` otherwise, the same two renderers the `drawer` and `modal` branches use. Width and title come along unchanged.
   - It is mounted in the `split` branch and, behind `formLayout === 'popover'`, in the default branch. No other branch renders it, so `drawer`, `modal` and `page` are untouched.
2. **No double surface.**
   - `handleCreate` clears `selectedRecord`, and both beside-surfaces still require `isFormOpen && selectedRecord`, so a create form never draws twice.
   - `handleRowClick` (under `split` / `popover`), `handleEdit` and `handleView` set a record and a mode other than `create`, so an existing record still opens beside the list. After a create closes, `formMode` stays `create` behind a closed drawer or dialog until the next row click moves it, which renders nothing visible.
3. **`page` routes first.** `layout === 'page'` with `onNavigate` still hands New to the router in `handleCreate`, before any state is set. Only `page` without `onNavigate` reaches the helper and takes the drawer. The code comment says so.
4. **Both sources of the mode.** `formLayout` reads `navigationConfig`, which is the active named view's `navigation` when one is authored (objectui#10885 member 4). The named-view pin puts a named `split` over a node `modal` and gets the drawer, so the node's replaced `navigation` does not pick the surface.
5. **Pins** (6 rows):
   - Three fix rows: the node's `split`, the node's `popover` with `layout: 'modal'` (asserted in a dialog and not in the drawer), and a named `split`.
   - Three controls: `drawer` New unchanged, a `split` row click, and a `split` Edit. Both beside controls assert the `Tasks Detail` panel, the grid still mounted, and no dialog.
   - The dev's base leg gives 3 failed / 3 passed, exactly the fix rows. The ablation of the helper's body turns exactly those three red. The surface mutation (always the drawer) turns only the `layout: 'modal'` row red, so that assertion is live.
6. **Docs.**
   - The dated note is on the pending `.changeset/10885-object-view-route2-named-view-rest.md`. It is still pending on `main` at blob `1a1249e244`, and its front matter is unchanged. It names the sentence it supersedes, "the New button opens no form", which appears in that changeset.
   - The README and docs pages add the same paragraph under Opening a record, plus one sentence in the named-view paragraph. Their "surface and width of the record, create and edit forms, follow the active named view" is now qualified.
   - The order was wrong on one point, and the dev measured it: it said the README and docs pages carry the "opens no form" sentence, but they carry 0 hits. The dev amended the sentence the fix does make false instead.
7. **One phrase is looser than its own gloss.**
   - The new changeset and the dated note say the create form opens on "the surface the node uses with no `navigation`", then gloss it: the modal for `layout: 'modal'`, the drawer otherwise.
   - For `layout: 'page'` without `onNavigate`, the node with no `navigation` opens nothing. That is the dev's first out-of-scope finding, so the phrase overstates for that one case. The gloss after the colon is exact and matches the code, so a reader who acts on it gets the shipped behaviour.
   - This does not block. The seat files that `page` case with its own carrier.

### ② Semver level

`'@object-ui/plugin-view': patch`, and `Clause-②: no` holds. `renderCreateSurface` is local to the component, and no declared type, accepted key or export moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **CI:** this record posts only after the eight required checks at `0d122bf345` are final and green. The landing queue gates on them and re-runs `git merge-tree` against current `main` first.
- **`Bundle Analysis`:** red. `main` is 18 B over the console eager-closure ceiling (objectui#10996), and this PR adds +35 gzip bytes, measured by the dev on a console build at base and at head. It is not a required check. One standing-down comment says so on the PR.
- **Merge-tree (dev):** clean against `main` `ad0310fb57`. That includes PR objectui#11010, which touched app-shell only.
- **Governed surfaces:** `check-governed-queue-guard --test` reports NOT GOVERNED on the 6 paths. The PR's own `Governed Surface Queue Guard` check-run decides.
- **State:** draft, with assignee `os-elon-musk`. There is no `needs:contract-review` label, which fits `Clause-②: no`.
